card.title: Slowest Snacking Speed
card.sub: Binary Search on the Answer · Medium

a1.cap: There are piles[i] snacks in pile i. Each hour you pick one pile and eat up to k snacks from it (if it has fewer, you finish it and wait for the hour to end). Return the smallest integer speed k that lets you finish all piles within h hours.
a1.say: There are piles at i snacks in pile i. Each hour you pick one pile and eat up to k snacks from it (if it has fewer, you finish it and wait for the hour to end). Return the smallest integer speed k that lets you finish all piles within h hours.

lines: There are piles[i] snacks in pile i. Each hour you pick one pile and eat up to k snacks from it (if it has fewer, you finish it and wait for the hour to end). Return the smallest integer speed k that lets you finish all piles within h hours.

a1.cap: For example, with piles = [3,6,7,11], h = 8, the answer is 4.
a1.say: For example, with piles equals 3, 6, 7, 11, h equals 8, the answer is 4.

a1.cap: Faster speeds always finish sooner, so the possible speeds split into "too slow" then "fast enough". Binary search for the first speed that is fast enough.
For a guessed speed, the hours needed are the sum over piles of pile divided by speed, rounded up.
Let's walk through it with piles = [3,6,7,11], h = 8.
a1.say: Let's walk through it with piles equals 3, 6, 7, 11, h equals 8.

a1.cap: At speed 6 we need 6 hours, which fits in 8. Try slower.
At speed 3 we need 10 hours, more than 8. Go faster.
At speed 5 we need 8 hours, which fits in 8. Try slower.
At speed 4 we need 8 hours, which fits in 8. Try slower.
Time complexity is O(n log m) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n log m and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Binary Search on the Answer approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
